##### DAGs and SWIGs

Under an independence assumption such as single-world independence (@def-single-world), which the FFRCISTG makes, an NPSEM implies a set of conditional independencies among its random variables. In principle these can be deduced from the structural equations themselves, by tracing which disturbances and which earlier variables each variable depends on. It turns out that queries like this are much simpler to answer through a graphical representation of the NPSEM than through the NPSEM itself, however. The directed acyclic graph relative to which the NPSEM is defined communicates them efficiently.

A causal directed acyclic graph (DAG) (@fig-fully-connected-dag) is a graph whose nodes represent the variables in an NPSEM (@eq-fully-connected-dag). Directed edges point from the arguments to the result of each structural equation.

{{< include ___figures/fig-fully-connected-dag.qmd >}}

A single-world intervention graph (SWIG) (@fig-fully-connected-swig) is a DAG whose nodes represent the variables in the interventional data model included in a causal model (@eq-fully-connected-swig). Directed edges point from the arguments to the result of each structural equation. It is built from the causal DAG by splitting each intervened node in two: its natural value (for example $A_1$), which keeps the node's incoming edges, and the value set by the intervention (for example $a_1$), which keeps its outgoing edges.

{{< include ___figures/fig-fully-connected-swig.qmd >}}

DAGs and SWIGs are useful because they encode statistical relationships among the variables in an NPSEM through a set of graphical rules called [d-separation](#sec-d-separation). Under an FFRCISTG, the law of the observed variables factorizes over the DAG as $p(\mathbf v) = \prod_{V \in \mathbf V} p(v \mid \mathbf{pa}_V)$, so two variables that are [d-separated](#sec-d-separation) given a set $\mathbf B$ in the DAG are conditionally independent given $\mathbf B$. The converse needs an extra assumption (faithfulness). In the SWIG, d-separation gives conditional independencies among the counterfactual variables in the same way.
